storylines.title: A glacier collapsed with no earthquake to warn anyone it was coming
storylines.observation: A glacial lake high in the Himalayas drained without warning on Aug 26, sending a 100km wall of water, ice and mud through Nepal and Tibet — killing 600+ in Nepal alone, with thousands still missing, including hundreds of foreign trekkers.
storylines.question: What do you build a warning system for when the disaster itself generates the only signal that it's happening?
storylines.hidden_question: Is a hazard 'unpredictable' because it truly can't be foreseen, or because nobody built the instrument that would have seen it coming?
storylines.pattern: a disaster whose only warning sign is the disaster itself
storylines.why_now: The barrier lake that formed from the collapse forced rescuers to briefly suspend operations Saturday over fears of a second flood, before resuming. Nepal's toll has climbed to 675 dead with ~2,500 still missing, including 90 Americans; Tibet's toll rose to 16 dead with 558 missing. Nepal's army has aerial-evacuated 2,500+ people so far, and the US has pledged $3.6M in emergency aid.

history.note: Rescue briefly suspended Saturday over fears of a second flood from the collapse's barrier lake. Nepal's toll: 675 dead, ~2,500 missing (incl. 90 Americans). Tibet: 16 dead, 558 missing. 2,500+ rescued by air; US pledges $3.6M in aid.

USGS confirms the seismic signal was generated by the collapse itself, not a preceding quake. Nepal's toll: 633 dead, ~3,000 missing. Tibet: 7 dead, 554 missing, 260 of them foreign. A shrinking barrier lake now threatens a second flood.

storylines.title: A telescope built to find what we don't have a name for yet
storylines.observation: NASA's Roman Space Telescope, cleared for launch after its final readiness review, carries a mirror the size of Hubble's but surveys roughly a hundred times more sky per shot — built for breadth rather than depth, to catch what narrower instruments would miss entirely.
storylines.question: What do you build when the thing you're looking for doesn't have a name yet?
storylines.hidden_question: Is breadth or depth the better strategy for finding something genuinely unexpected?
storylines.pattern: wide-survey instrument built to catch what narrow ones would miss
storylines.why_now: Liftoff happened exactly on schedule at 7:26am EDT, and both Falcon Heavy side boosters stuck flawless return landings at Kennedy Space Center. Roman has now separated from the upper stage and achieved trans-Lagrange insertion — it's actually on its way, a roughly 30-day cruise to the Sun-Earth L2 point where its wide-field survey mission begins.

history.note: Liftoff succeeded at 7:26am EDT; both Falcon Heavy side boosters landed back at Kennedy Space Center, and Roman separated cleanly, now on its ~30-day cruise to the Sun-Earth L2 point.
Liftoff set for 7:26am EDT from Pad 39A; after launch, Roman begins a ~30-day cruise to the Sun-Earth L2 point, 930,000 miles out, to begin its wide-field survey mission.

storylines.title: Armenia jails its most prominent opposition leader the day after declaring for Europe
storylines.observation: Armenian prosecutors detained former president and opposition-bloc leader Robert Kocharyan on corruption charges one day after PM Pashinyan announced Armenia's EU membership bid — raising the question of whether the case is accountability or a rival cleared from the board at a pivotal moment.
storylines.question: How do you tell an anti-corruption prosecution from a political purge when both can look identical from the outside?
storylines.hidden_question: Does the timing itself become evidence, even when the underlying charges might be entirely legitimate?
storylines.pattern: a legal crackdown landing at the exact moment it most benefits the government's freedom of maneuver
storylines.why_now: The Kremlin has now weighed in directly on both threads at once: Russian FM Lavrov criticized Armenia's plan to hold its referendum only after formally applying to the EU as "sitting on two chairs," arguing Yerevan should choose honestly given $6B+ in EAEU trade — while Armenia's Security Council chief says he hopes Russia won't bring up Kocharyan's case at all, tacitly conceding it's now on Moscow's table.
storylines.season_or_time_context: ahead of Armenia's EU accession push

history.note: Lavrov himself weighed in, calling Armenia's referendum-after-application plan "sitting on two chairs" given $6B+ in EAEU trade; Armenia's Security Council chief now hopes Russia won't raise Kocharyan's case at all.

Pashinyan has added a referendum to the EU-accession process; Armenia's Security Council secretary says the prospect alone is enough to upset Moscow, as Russian commentary frames the pivot as an unaffordable trade.

storylines.title: Congo tests whether a peace agreement is real
storylines.observation: Nine months after a US-brokered framework, a ceasefire verification mission has deployed to eastern Congo — pairing Congolese army and M23 officers with regional and international observers to check whether a signed truce holds up on the ground.
storylines.question: How long does it take a peace agreement to become an actual peace, and who gets to decide when it has?
storylines.hidden_question: Is verification a technical formality, or the point where a peace deal actually gets tested?
storylines.pattern: the gap between a signed agreement and a verified one
storylines.why_now: The fragility the mission exists to fix keeps playing out in real time: M23 accuses government drone strikes of killing civilians near Minembwe, the DRC accuses M23 of killing 300+ people in June-July, and the two sides only just agreed, in Aug 17-21 talks, on a standardized way to even report these competing claims — neither side's account can stand alone.

history.note: M23 accuses DRC drone strikes of killing civilians near Minembwe; DRC accuses M23 of killing 300+ in June-July. The two sides agreed in Aug 17-21 talks on a standardized way to even report these competing claims.

storylines.title: Canada weighs retaliation in trade dispute with the US
storylines.observation: A long-standing trade relationship between neighbors is being renegotiated through tariffs and countermeasures rather than talks — testing how much economic pain each side will absorb before returning to the table.
storylines.question: When does retaliation become the negotiating strategy rather than a response to one?
storylines.hidden_question: Can two deeply integrated economies actually decouple, or does retaliation just relocate the cost?
storylines.pattern: escalation as bargaining posture between interdependent economies
storylines.why_now: Ottawa is now backstopping its own retaliation: alongside the Sept 8 counter-tariffs on 700+ US goods worth roughly $20B, it announced a C$7.5B domestic support package for the workers and businesses its own countermeasures will hit hardest — retaliation with a built-in admission of its domestic cost.
storylines.season_or_time_context: ongoing trade dispute, ahead of Sept 8 tariffs

history.note: Ottawa paired its Sept 8 retaliatory tariffs on 700+ US goods with a C$7.5B domestic support package for the workers and businesses its own countermeasures will hit hardest.

storylines.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions raise new Iranian demands
storylines.observation: A quarter of the world's seaborne oil passes through a chokepoint controlled by a single actor's threats — pricing in a shutdown that has never actually happened but is never fully dismissed either.
storylines.question: How does a market price a threat that is credible but has never been carried out?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the strait's value as leverage greater than its value as a functioning waterway?
storylines.pattern: chokepoint leverage priced as permanent risk premium
storylines.why_now: Iran and Oman have reached a revenue-sharing toll deal on a temporary shipping corridor and are discussing a permanent one — but the strait won't actually reopen until the US fulfills its commitments under an interim June peace deal that has since lapsed. Meanwhile Washington's new sanctions campaign, dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast," has drawn a threat from Tehran to retaliate "in a seismic manner."

history.note: Iran and Oman reached a revenue-sharing toll deal, discussing a permanent corridor — but the strait stays closed pending the US honoring its own lapsed June peace deal, as Washington's new sanctions draw threats of "seismic" Iranian retaliation.
